card.title: Outfeel the Room
card.instruction: Answer every fear, sacrifice, or disappointment with one of your own that deserves more attention.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One sleepless night before your interview? I've been awake all week worrying about mine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I just need you to practise questions with me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask why I left my last job. You'll understand why my interview is harder.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm scared I'll cry. Let's use your practice time to get me through the greeting.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 sleeplessness outbids B's, A3 takes over practice with a harder past-job story and A5 greater crying fear takes B's allotted time.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 practice request causes A3 reversing question roles; B4 freezing fear causes A5 competing fear and time appropriation.

relationship.evidence: B2 asks for needed practical help and B4 states the vulnerability motivating it.

heightening.evidence: B4 direct need is met by A5 a supposedly greater need that consumes the support requested for B.

specificity.evidence: A1 competing interviews and B2 rehearsal establish attention and time as the contested resources.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 using your practice time makes the attention displacement concrete rather than only a bigger-suffering claim.
